implementation_notes: Kotlin mud is usually a single Gradle module, which means the compiler cannot help: everything in one source set, one test source set, and no boundary the build can enforce. The practical consolidation is to introduce Gradle modules or at least package-level `internal` visibility so the build starts refusing the widest dependencies, and then to narrow gradually. Kotlin's extension functions and top-level declarations make the mud worse than it looks, because a helper declared `internal` in one file is reachable from every file in the module.
idiom_name: one Gradle module with a root package containing every subsystem
pitfalls: `internal` is module-scoped, so in a single-module project it protects nothing — the boundary has to be a build boundary.
Kotlin DSL build scripts can themselves accumulate into a mud of shared configuration that every subproject depends on.
`typealias` chains across packages make the import graph look simple while the real coupling stays.
